 A Cybertruck owner details his frustrating repair experience after a major accident. He says his truck has been at the Tesla repair center for 5 months and has cost his insurance provider $63,000, yet the truck still does not work.
 Advertising 
 October 19, 2026 - 9:00AM EDT 
 By: Tinsae Aregay 
 Matt, a Cybertruck owner from Florida, says his truck was involved in a major accident five months ago, and despite $63,000 in repair bills and all that time, it still isn't working properly.
 Since the accident, Matt says he’s been told seven times that the truck was fixed, only for it to fail again on his way home from the Tesla service center.
 Matt mentions that even though the repair process has been frustrating, he’s grateful to be alive and credits the Cybertruck for saving his life.
 Matt says he was driving on the highway when another vehicle rear-ended him, spinning him across five lanes and into the path of a second vehicle, which then hit him.
 Matt says that even though his Cybertruck spun around 270 degrees and was hit twice by two vehicles driving well over the speed limit, the truck did not roll over.
 Matt shares his harrowing experience on the  Cybertruck Owners Club forum.
 He writes…
 “Well, the worst thing happened, but grateful to still be alive thanks to the Cybertruck. It certainly prevented me from rolling over. 
 FSD did an amazing job navigating while spinning 270 degrees across 5 lanes of highway at 78 mph. 
 My truck was targeted by two vehicles as I was headed south on the highway. The first vehicle hit the rear passenger quarter at approximately 115 mph, then the 2nd vehicle hit the driver's side. 
 Advertising 
 A third car, apparently unrelated, was involved. All three vehicles, their drivers, and their 12 passengers were uninsured. Go figure. The drivers turned out to be undocumented immigrants. Go figure. 
 The truck has been at the Tesla collision center for 5 months and has been deemed ready 7 times. 
 Each time, regrettably, something else fails, either immediately upon test drive (service vehicles are limited to 8 mph) or on my way home. 
 It's been a variety of things, approximately $63k in damage so far... getting up there. 
 This week, the computer failed and caused all sorts of weird and crazy issues, including the high beams not turning off, locks, cameras, GPS, and a multitude of systems failing. 
 It's now being repaired under warranty, but at the collision center, not the service center. 
 My question to everyone is this. Assuming the latest issue with my Cybertruck gets fixed (I am losing a little hope at this point), how reliable is it? 
 What else should I look out for? Do I even accept and sign off on the paperwork, since the claim is still open? 
 My insurance, GEICO, has paid everything with little objection. I wasn't at fault, have no prior accidents, and I'm in South Florida. 
 Advertising 
 It originally had 8,000 miles and is a 2024 top-of-the-line Performance Foundation Series Cybertruck. 
 This is definitely not ideal, and looking at the comments, fellow Cybertruck owners shared their thoughts.
 A fellow Cybertruck owner, Art, writes…
 “Most importantly, you made it through the accident. If it was on I-95, I can feel your pain because there are road incidents every day. 
 As for the truck, I would be more concerned about driving alignment issues. If it’s not pulling to one side and FSD is consistent, that is a major feat after an accident. 
 The electronics should be sortable, since most components are designed to be interchangeable. Hope it gets sorted out for you.” 
 A second Cybertruck owner writes…
 “Wow... What were they targeting you for? A payout? 115 mph with passengers? Hope they were deported. 
 I know it'll suck to lose FSD, but you should definitely total it. There will always be issues with it.” 
 Overall, having to wait 5 months after an accident and more than $63,000 in repair bills isn't ideal. However, please let me know what you think in the comments.
